question: Under Iowa's child care center rules (441 IAC 109), what is the minimum staff-to-child ratio for children aged two weeks to two years at a licensed child care center in Iowa? Give the number of children per staff member.
quote: Age of children ... Two weeks to two years ... Minimum ratio of staff to children ... One to every 4 children
notes: Youngest band in the table. The ratio for children under two must be kept even at nap time (109.8(2)“h”). If a child under two is in a combined 18-month-to-3-year group, the group ratio is 1:7 (109.8(2)“c”).

question: Under Iowa's child care center rules (441 IAC 109), what is the minimum staff-to-child ratio for three-year-olds at a licensed child care center in Iowa? Give the number of children per staff member.
quote: Three years ... Minimum ratio of staff to children ... One to every 10 children
notes: Combined groups of three-, four- and five-year-olds may use 1:12 (109.8(2)“b”). Children 18 months to three years may be combined (109.8(2)“c”).

question: Under Iowa's child care center rules (441 IAC 109), what is the minimum staff-to-child ratio for four-year-olds at a licensed child care center in Iowa? Give the number of children per staff member.
quote: Four years ... Minimum ratio of staff to children ... One to every 12 children
notes: Combined groups of children four and older may use the ratio for the age of the majority (109.8(2)“a”).

question: Under Iowa's child care center rules (441 IAC 109), what is the minimum staff-to-child ratio for the oldest age band in the ratio table, children 'ten years and over', at a licensed child care center in Iowa? Give the number of children per staff member.
quote: Ten years and over ... Minimum ratio of staff to children ... One to every 20 children
notes: The band 'Five years to ten years' is 1:15. As printed, the two bands overlap at age ten. Combined groups of children five and older use the ratio for the age of the majority (109.8(2)“e”). The school-age ratio may be exceeded for up to four hours on late-start, early-dismissal or weather days (109.8(2)“m”).

question: How is the maximum group size for children, including four-year-olds, set for a licensed child care center in Iowa under 441 IAC 109?
answer: It is determined in collaboration with the state fire marshal, based on a review of health and safety requirements. The rule sets no fixed number.
quote: 109.8(3) Group size. Group size is determined in collaboration with the state fire marshal and will be assigned based on the review of health and safety requirements.
notes: No numeric group size by age appears in chapter 109. Maximum capacity is printed on the license and group sizes by age go in annual inspection reports.

question: What is the minimum age for a staff person counted in the staff-to-child ratio at a licensed child care center in Iowa?
quote: 109.8(1) Staff requirements. Persons counted as part of the staff ratio must meet the following requirements: a. Staff persons must be at least 16 years of age.
notes: Staff under 18 may not be the sole provider on the premises or transport children. Without an adult present they may care only for school-aged children (109.8(1)“b”).

question: Under Iowa's child care center rules (441 IAC 109), how many total points, earned through a combination of education, experience, and child development-related training, must the director of a licensed child care center in Iowa have achieved?
quote: Has achieved a total of 100 points obtained through a combination of education, experience, and child development-related training
notes: The director must also be at least 21, have a high school diploma or GED, have one business administration course or 12 contact hours of administrative training or one year of administrative experience, and hold pediatric CPR, pediatric first aid and Iowa mandatory reporter training (109.6(1)“a”–“d”).

question: After their first year of employment, how many contact hours of professional development must staff at a licensed child care center in Iowa receive each year?
quote: (2) Staff must receive six contact hours of professional development annually from one or more of the subject areas
notes: First-year staff need ten contact hours (109.7(2)“a”). Directors and on-site supervisors need eight contact hours a year (109.7(2)“b”(3)). Coaching may cover up to half of the annual requirement (109.7(5)“b”).

question: How many square feet of usable floor space per child must a program room provide at a licensed child care center in Iowa, in a room where floor space occupied by cribs is not counted as usable floor space?
quote: The program room size must be a minimum of 80 square feet of useable floor space or sufficient floor space to provide 35 square feet of useable floor space per child.
notes: In rooms where floor space occupied by cribs is counted, 40 sq ft per child is required. Kitchens, bathrooms, halls, lobbies and storage areas do not count.

question: A licensed child care center in Iowa must have an adjacent outdoor program area large enough for at least 30 percent of its enrollment capacity at any one time. How many square feet per child must that area provide?
quote: Centers must have a safe outdoor program area adjacent to the center, with sufficient square footage to accommodate at least 30 percent of the enrollment capacity at any one time at 75 square feet per child.
notes: 75 sq ft per child applies to 30% of enrollment capacity at one time, not to full licensed capacity. The department may waive the outdoor requirement for programs of three hours or less (109.11(4)“c”).

question: At a licensed child care center in Iowa, what training must a staff member have completed before giving a child medication?
answer: Preservice/orientation training that includes medication administration.
quote: A child care staff member shall not provide medications to a child if the staff member has not completed preservice/orientation training that includes medication administration.
notes: Staff must also be over 18 to give medication (109.10(1)“a”). The center needs written procedures covering authorization, and a notation is required each day an authorization is in effect, but the rule does not say who must sign the authorization. Long-term authorizations may not exceed the prescription's duration (109.10(1)“d”).

question: How often must a licensed child care center in Iowa practice and document its fire emergency procedures (fire drills)?
quote: Emergency plan procedures must be practiced and documented at least once a month for fire and for tornado.
notes: Tornado drills are also required monthly.

question: For how long must a licensed child care center in Iowa keep records of its fire and tornado drill practice?
answer: For the current year and the previous year.
quote: Records on the practice of fire and tornado drills must be maintained for the current and previous year.
notes: This is the only record retention period found in chapter 109.

question: In what position must infants be placed for sleep at a licensed child care center in Iowa?
quote: (1) Infants shall always be placed on their backs for sleep.
notes: Applies to infants under one year. Another position requires a signed physician or physician associate authorization giving the medical reason and an expiration date (109.12(4)“e”(7)).

question: Within what time must a licensed child care center in Iowa report a child's serious injury to the department?
quote: (1) Serious injuries must be reported to the department within 24 hours of the incident.
notes: Serious injury as defined in Iowa Code 702.18. Parents, guardians and legal custodians must be told verbally right away (109.10(8)“b”).

question: What immunization document must be on file for each child enrolled at a licensed child care center in Iowa?
answer: A signed and dated valid Certificate of Immunization, Certificate of Immunization Exemption, or Provisional Certificate of Immunization.
quote: Signed and dated valid Certificate of Immunization, Certificate of Immunization Exemption, or Provisional Certificate of Immunization, provided by the department must be on file for each child enrolled as required by 641—Chapter 7.
notes: The rule sets no deadline in days; the certificate must be on file for every enrolled child under 641—Chapter 7. For children not yet in kindergarten, the physical exam is due at enrollment and no later than four weeks after admission (109.9(2)“i”).

question: Within how many months of starting employment must every staff member at a licensed child care center in Iowa be certified in infant, child, and adult CPR and first aid?
quote: During their first three months of employment, all staff must receive the following training: ... c. Certification in infant, child, and adult CPR. ... d. Certification in infant, child, and adult first aid.
notes: Applies to all staff. Certifications must be kept current after the first year (109.7(2)“b”(1)). The director must hold pediatric CPR and pediatric first aid before approval (109.6(1)“d”).

searched: spacing (only 'Sufficient spacing must be maintained.' in 109.11(2)“b”, no distance)

question: For how long is a license issued to a licensed child care center in Iowa that shows compliance with the licensing laws and rules?
quote: An applicant showing compliance with center licensing laws and these rules, including department approval of center plans and procedures and submission of the regulatory fee as specified in subrule 109.2(5) to the department by the date due, shall be issued a license for 24 months.
notes: A new license is needed when the center moves, expands, is remodeled to change capacity, or changes ownership.

question: During nap time at a licensed child care center in Iowa, when staff ratio coverage can be maintained in the center, to what may the staff ratio be reduced in rooms where children two years of age and older are resting?
answer: One staff member per room where children are resting.
quote: Staff ratio requirements may be reduced to one staff member per room where children are resting and staff ratio coverage can be maintained in the center. The staff ratio must always be maintained for children under two years of age.
notes: Not allowed for children under two. At least one staff member must be in every room where children rest.

question: For a center-sponsored activity away from the licensed facility involving six or more children, how many staff beyond the required staff ratio must a licensed child care center in Iowa provide at minimum?
quote: Any child care center-sponsored program activity involving six or more children conducted away from the licensed facility shall provide a minimum of one additional staff over the required staff ratio for the protection of the children.
notes: At least one staff member on a field trip must be over 18.

question: When a licensed child care center in Iowa combines three-, four-, and five-year-olds in one group, what staff-to-child ratio may it use? Give the number of children per staff member.
quote: Combinations of age groupings for children three, four, and five years of age may be allowed with a ratio of one staff member to every 12 children.
notes: Groups of children four and older may instead use the ratio for the age of the majority (109.8(2)“a”).

question: When school classes start late, are dismissed early, or are canceled because of inclement weather or structural damage, for at most how many hours in a day may a licensed child care center in Iowa exceed the school-age staff ratio?
quote: the ratio for school-age children may be exceeded for a period of no more than four hours during a day when school classes start late or are dismissed early or canceled due to inclement weather or structural damage
notes: Only for children already enrolled, and only if the center stays within its licensed capacity.

question: For a period of two hours or less at the beginning and end of the hours of operation of a licensed child care center in Iowa, what is the largest number of children one staff member may care for alone?
quote: For a period of two hours or less at the beginning and end of the center's hours of operation, one staff member may care for eight or fewer children, provided no more than four of the children are under two years of age and there are no more than eight children in the center.
notes: No more than four of the children may be under two, and there may be no more than eight children in the whole center. Otherwise, when more than eight children are present, at least two staff must be present (109.8(2)“i”).
